analysis.title: High Yield & Loan Strategy: Technicals to remain firm in '27 as AI capex shifts to Pvt Credit
key_insights: BofA expects credit technicals to stay firm in 2027 as lower volatility and rates after the election support demand. In HY, higher flows plus marginally higher supply improve technicals. In loans, refinancing-led supply rises and demand grows modestly, so technicals soften from current levels but stay positive.

Credit-funded AI capex is forecast at about $685bn in 2027 vs $523bn in 2026 (+31%), then $531bn in 2028 (-23%), making 2027 the peak for debt-funding needs. Private/bilateral financing roughly doubles to $353bn (+94%), public IG falls 8% to $262bn, and HY+BSL rises 23% to $70bn from a small base.

Private financing of AI capex debt is estimated to cross 50% of total annual supply in 2027, helped by unrated XPV platform debt financing and investor pushback in public markets that has made public debt costlier. IG investor demand could flow into private XPV deals.
Downside risk to the AI debt forecasts comes from a possible slowdown in AI infrastructure projects after the Blue Wave midterm result, which would reduce capex and debt funding needs.

Oversupply has been mostly an IG issue (2026 running +30% y/y), while HY supply is flat y/y and loans are running -10%. The post-summer widening in LevFin came from relative value vs IG (supply and rates vol) and beta underperformance on doubts about AI profitability and capex durability, not from technicals.

Primary market access is deteriorating at the margin. The last two weeks showed the first impact on primary access, limited so far to CCCs. BofA warns that a buyer's strike in the primary could hurt corporate health if negative sentiment persists.

HY gross issuance is forecast to rise 3% to $340bn in 2027, driven by refinancings +28% to $200bn, with M&A/LBO/dividend flat at $65bn and AI-related issuance at $50bn. 2026 is on track for about $330bn, below BofA's $360bn forecast because higher rates curbed refinancing.

HY net supply is forecast +27% to $71bn and net demand +16% to $148bn, so demand net of supply improves 8% to $77bn. Retail flows are expected at $20bn in 2027 vs $3bn in 2026, while coupon demand rises 3% to $128bn.

HY calls/tenders are projected at 13.7% of the index ($208bn, -2%) as higher 5-year yields reduce the incentive for early takeouts. Fallen angels are forecast at $35bn (+30%), as BBB notional trading at BB spreads rose to 3.2% from 0.7%, and rising stars at $70bn (+3%).

Loan gross issuance is forecast +18% to $470bn, with refinancings +77% to $250bn on the near-term maturity wall (highest since 2013) and M&A/LBO/dividend -20% to $175bn. BofA haircuts its quant refinancing estimate of about $350bn for rate volatility and for maturities ending in defaults or LMEs.

Loan technicals soften: demand net of supply falls from $44bn LTM to $19bn in 2027, as prepayments rise to $340bn and net supply reaches $130bn against $149bn of demand ($49bn net CLO creation, $106bn coupons, $6bn retail outflows).

Loan repricings are muted. YTD repricing volume is $257bn, down 43% y/y, and the share of loans above par fell from 46% in September to 7% in late October before recovering to 15%. Loans' exposure to AI intermediation is cited as a concern.
AI-related issuance totals $632bn YTD ($308bn IG, $53bn HY, $16bn institutional loans, $252bn private credit/direct lending/bilateral), after $50bn from Microsoft, Meta and Oracle over the past week.

IG AI-related spreads are 148bp (new wides of 155bp on Nov 2) vs 77bp for comparable ex-AI bonds, a 71bp premium. HY AI-related spreads are 431bp, 54bp wider since Oct 28 and inside the record 445bp of Oct 23, with the AI vs ex-AI premium at 218bp vs a record 227bp.

IG shows little crowding-out from AI supply, with ex-AI spreads within their 12-month range. In HY, ex-AI spreads have started to come under pressure, overlapping with record chunky new issuance and a spike in rates volatility. BofA's prior work attributes this largely to a duration shock, but the reaction function could change in a risk-off tape.

Weekly HY recap: spreads widened 18bp WoW to 332bp (Bs +33bp, CCCs -10bp), total return +0.20% (BBs +30bp, CCCs -38bp). HY funds took in $0.9bn WTD, MTD issuance is $7.4bn (73% BB, 27% B). HY CSI is flat at 47.2%.

Weekly loan recap: loans returned 0.37% WTD (Bs 0.41%, CCCs 0.34%, BBs 0.27%) at a 94.8pt index price. WTD demand was $5.37bn vs $3.43bn of issuance, and YTD demand net of supply is +$97.5bn vs +$89.1bn a year ago. Loan CSI is 57.7%.

Credit quality: net HY downgrades were $13.3bn on the week, led by Cloud Software Group ($6.8bn), Whirlpool ($6.3bn) and Mercer ($1.2bn). Telecom Italia became a rising star, and YTD rising stars of $61.0bn exceed fallen angels of $37.0bn. No HY or BSL defaults MTD, YTD defaults are $16.8bn HY and $24.4bn loans, with recoveries of 37 cents (HY) and 54 cents (loans).

Dispersion in HY: the worst CSI decile (D10) has returned -15.1% YTD in excess of the index and -4.68% over one month, while CCC loans are -8.39% YTD. CoreWeave screens cheap to its CSI-implied OAS (1,099bp vs 834bp estimate) while Charter, Whirlpool and Gray TV screen rich.

CLO AAA primary spreads are 125bp, unchanged from the start of the year. CLO arbitrage is 219bp as of Oct 30 vs 190bp at the start of the year and a March peak of 231bp. BofA forecasts net CLO creation of about $50bn in 2027 (+5%) with gross CLO issuance -15% to $335bn.

market_movers.rationale: CoreWeave debt screens cheap in BofA's rich/cheap screen, with OAS of 1,099bp vs a CSI-implied 834bp. BofA notes the screen is not a recommended list. HY bond price fell 4.9% on the week.

Charter screens rich to its CSI-implied OAS (290bp vs 626bp estimate). It also appears as a fallen angel candidate (CCO Holdings, BBB3) and a downgrade candidate. BofA notes the screen is not a recommendation.
Whirlpool was downgraded one notch this week ($6.3bn of debt) and screens rich to its CSI-implied OAS (610bp vs 854bp).
Oracle (BBB2, $119bn of debt) is on the fallen angel watchlist and issued $10bn of IG bonds on Nov 2 at spreads of 240-335bp.
Caesars bonds were downgraded one notch in the recent rating actions table.
Medical Properties Trust was downgraded one notch. Its bonds fell 11.3% on the week and it sits in the worst CSI decile.

sector_views.rationale: Media led MTD HY gains (+116bps) but had the largest 4-week downgrades, including Paramount (Skydance) which pulled the 12-week net upgrade figure to a one-year low.
Travel (+110bps) and Retail (+104bps) were among MTD HY leaders.
Energy and Tech were the weakest HY sectors this month at -21bps each. Energy and Capital Goods led 4-week upgrades.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Spreads widened 18bp WoW, with Bs +33bp and CCCs -10bp.
Retraced from 155bp wides on Nov 2. The premium over ex-AI IG (77bp) is 71bp.
Inside the record 445bp of Oct 23 but 54bp wider since Oct 28.
Flat WoW. Dispersion and volatility drove stress after summer, with the first primary access impact in CCCs.
Flat WoW, as higher credit access offset lower risk tolerance.
Net demand of $148bn (+16%) outpaces it, so HY technicals improve 8% to $77bn.
Down from $44bn LTM, so loan technicals stay positive but the cushion narrows.
Up 31% from $523bn in 2026 and then down 23% to $531bn in 2028, making 2027 the peak.

macro_indicators.reading: market has moved from expecting cuts to expecting hikes
macro_indicators.interpretation: Higher rates cut refinancing volume in 2026 and reduced calls/tenders, though BofA expects lower rates and volatility after the election to support 2027 demand.

risk_factors: A buyer's strike in the primary market for CCC and weaker credits could limit funding and hurt corporate health, a causality flip BofA has seen before.
AI profitability and capex durability doubts could keep pressuring HY AI-related spreads, which sit near record wides (431bp vs 445bp record).
HY ex-AI spreads may start to reflect AI supply crowding-out if risk-off sentiment persists.
Higher rates and rates volatility may keep suppressing refinancing and M&A, and a rising share of near-term loan maturities may end in defaults or LMEs rather than new issuance.
The Blue Wave midterm result could change Fed hike expectations or lower GDP expectations, increasing retail loan outflows beyond the forecast $6bn.
A slowdown in AI infrastructure projects would lower capex and debt-market funding versus the $685bn forecast.
CCC loan and bond weakness remains deep: CCC loans are -8.39% YTD, with CCC loan yields near 30%.
charts_described: Exhibit 2 table shows 2027 AI issuance of $685bn: hyperscalers $310bn (USD $183bn), private/bilateral $353bn, USD IG $262bn (-8% y/y), HY+BSL $70bn (+23% y/y).

Exhibit 10 shows HY 2027 forecast: gross issuance $340bn, maturities $25bn, calls/tenders $208bn, fallen angels $35bn, rising stars $70bn, net supply $71bn, flows $20bn, coupons $128bn, demand $148bn, demand net of supply $77bn.
Exhibit 16 shows the share of loans trading at par and above declined to 15% from a September high of 46%.
Exhibit 14 shows the share of loans maturing within two years at its highest level since 2013.
vol_and_positioning: Rates volatility spiked alongside record chunky HY new issuance, which BofA links to the recent HY ex-AI spread pressure, largely as a duration shock.
HY CSI inputs: equity vol 16.6 (42nd percentile), rates vol 0.9 (60.5th percentile), HY vol 5.0 (12.5th percentile). Dispersion is at the 66.5th percentile for HY and 95th percentile for loans.
Share of loans trading above par fell from 46% in September to 7% in late October, then recovered to 15%. BofA reads this as a gauge of investor risk tolerance.
HY effective bid-ask spreads were unchanged WoW at 0.33pt. Services and Healthcare traded at 1.5x their 3-month average volume.
HY internal demand is soft: $1.0bn of calls/maturities and $3.2bn of coupons this week, and about $3.3bn expected next week.
geopolitical: US midterm election result (the 'Blue Wave') is described as removing the election overhang, but a potential slowdown in AI infrastructure projects after it is a downside risk to AI debt supply forecasts. BofA also notes the result could change Fed hike forecasts or GDP expectations and push loan retail outflows higher.

tension_points.bull_case: Lower volatility and rates after the election, higher HY retail flows ($20bn vs $3bn) and a refi-driven supply rise lift HY demand net of supply 8% to $77bn, and loan technicals stay positive with a $19bn surplus.
tension_points.bear_case: Loan demand cushion narrows from $44bn to $19bn, and rate volatility, AI profitability doubts and a primary-market buyer's strike could curb access and keep spreads wide.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A buyer's strike in the primary that spreads beyond CCCs, or the Blue Wave result changing Fed hike forecasts or GDP expectations, would undercut the retail inflow and demand forecast.

tension_points.bull_case: Credit-funded AI capex reaches $685bn in 2027, with private credit absorbing most of the growth so public IG supply falls 8%, and credit fundamentals remain intact.
tension_points.bear_case: HY AI spreads are near record wides at 431bp, AI profitability and capex durability are questioned, and HY ex-AI spreads are starting to widen.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A slowdown in AI infrastructure projects after the Blue Wave result would cut capex and debt funding below the $685bn forecast.

theme_stances.key_argument: Refi-driven supply meets higher credit demand, improving HY technicals and keeping loan technicals positive.
